key_idea: Hahn–Banach gives a positive current P with an anti-invariant L^2 correction Q so that P+Q is closed. Quadratic mass growth and angular-coherence estimates then show that the positive-density part of P is closed. The final step pairs the closed current with the residual current supported on centers of zero density, which forces Q=0 and contradicts taming.
reason: The structure is careful and the main steps are visible: separation, a closed lift, mass growth from plurisubharmonic test functions, heat regularization, and the final pairing with the zero-density residual. The last step is a clever move. But the proof leans on many technical estimates (kernel decompositions, dyadic shells, commutator bounds, Jacobi-field corrections), so it reads more as a strong analytic campaign than a book proof.
recognized: no (an attempted proof of Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture in dimension four, in the style of Sullivan/Harvey–Lawson separation followed by geometric measure theory)
